title: Doxycycline and Nitazoxanide as a Candidate Immunomodulatory Combination for the Early Management of Ebola Disease Caused by Bundibugyo Virus
content: As of 11 November 2026, Bundibugyo virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo had produced 11,114 confirmed cases and 5,433 deaths, and in the latest WHO interval close to two of every three deaths were in communities, not treatment centres, especially among young children. No vaccine or treatment is approved for this species, and the agents in trials are monoclonal antibodies and direct-acting antivirals. In 2021, I proposed reclassifying COVID-19, Ebola virus disease and Nipah virus infection as a novel acute immune dysrhythmia syndrome. Read through it, the pathology described in Bundibugyo-infected macaques points to two arms: fatal animals showed myeloid hyperinflammation with raised interleukin-6 and myeloperoxidase, survivors showed transcripts consistent with an intact T cell response. Basing on that convergence I propose doxycycline and nitazoxanide as an early immunomodulatory combination, each on a different arm. Doxycycline inhibits matrix metalloproteinases at exposures achievable in man. Nitazoxanide amplifies RNA sensing and interferon signalling; its inhibition of Zaire ebolavirus in cell culture depends on RIG-I and PKR. However, none of this establishes efficacy in this disease. What it offers is a mechanism worth testing in two licensed, oral, inexpensive drugs on the shelf, the host-directed concentration unmeasured. I therefore ask for species-specific work to begin soonest: activity in relevant cells and in the macaque model, the unbound concentration-response relationship, and a two-by-two factorial evaluation, preclinical and clinical, powered for the interaction. For the patient who cannot reach a participating unit, I also call for monitored emergency use under the WHO framework, with every outcome recorded and reported. I strongly suggest that the search for safe immunomodulators is the one most likely to end in a drug available on the day it is needed.
